claim: apoF circulates as a proteolytic product of a larger precursor
finding: 29 kDa apoF purified from human HDL; cDNA encodes a 162-aa protein described as a proteolytic product of a larger protein
context: human plasma HDL; Hep G2 cDNA library
confidence: high; apparent mass not reconciled with 162 aa

claim: mature N-terminus is internal to the precursor
finding: 14-residue N-terminal sequence from the 33 kDa LDL band matches apoF cDNA; apoF almost exclusively on LDL
confidence: high; exact residue numbers not in abstract

claim: only three N-X-S/T sequons exist and only one is in the mature chain
finding: N118, N139 in propeptide 36-164; N267 the sole mature-chain sequon; no N-X-C sites

claim: the propeptide boundary is a furin-type convertase site
finding: RVGR161-164 is the only R-X-X-R outside the signal peptide; cleavage after R164 gives S165; R-X-X-R present in 120/122 mammals with mature length held near 158 aa
52 site-specific records: N118, N139, N267 plus O-sites T57, S59, T274, S302, S303; UniProt feature table lists 2
confidence: medium; site localisation quality varies by study

claim: propeptide-region sites are glycosylated on circulating material
finding: N118, N139 and N267 glycopeptides identified in 24 human serum samples
confidence: medium; cannot show the propeptide is still attached

claim: N118 glycopeptide is present in plasma
finding: N-glycopeptides quantified in human plasma and breast cancer cell-line secretome

claim: T274 on the mature chain is O-glycosylated
confidence: medium-high; the one UniProt ECO:0000269 glyco feature

claim: additional O-sites exist on both segments
finding: T57, S59 (propeptide) and S302, S303 (mature) localised
context: human kidney tissue, T cells, serum

finding: two plasma LTIP isoforms differing in carbohydrate content

claim: the acidic mature chain, not the precursor, is the physiological product
finding: hamster LTIP predicted pI 4.15, Mr ~16.4 kDa, matching human mature chain (pI 4.11, 17.4 kDa)

claim: a glycosite decorates a lipoprotein-binding amphipathic helix
finding: apoF predicted to lack strong amphipathic alpha helices; our moment profile agrees (N267 mu_H=0.10 vs chain max 0.47)

claim: apoF resides in discrete lipoprotein particles
finding: LpF, LpF:A-I and LpF:A-I:A-II isolated from normolipidemic plasma

claim: APOF interacts with the O-GalNAc transferase GALNT4
finding: BioPlex AP-MS association, sole basis of GO:0005515 on Q13790
